title: Request to reconsider my final grade
passage: Dear Professor Achebe, I'm writing about my final grade of C-. I know I missed three labs and never submitted the last report. But this semester has been incredibly hard: my car broke down twice and I've been working 30 hours a week. I really need a B to keep my scholarship. Could you please reconsider? Thank you, Jordan
cue: I really need a B to keep my scholarship
explanation: Jordan admits the missing work, then asks for a higher grade because of a hard semester and scholarship pressure. A grade measures the work completed; sympathy doesn't change that.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_emotion: Jordan isn't stirring pride or outrage; the request rests specifically on sympathy for a difficult semester.

source: Junior player to the line judge · Kestrel Point Open
passage: Come on, that ball was in! I've lost five matches in a row, my dad drove all night to get me here, and I've been playing through a sore wrist all week. Please, just give me this one point. I really need it.
cue: I've lost five matches in a row, my dad drove all night to get me here
explanation: The player wants the line call reversed because of a losing streak, a long drive and a sore wrist. None of that tells the judge where the ball actually landed.

whyNot.fal_red_herring: The player stays on the line call; the problem is offering hardships as the reason to change it.

title: Give this family a break
passage: Service was slow and my pasta arrived lukewarm. But the owner told us his wife has been ill and he's running the kitchen alone most nights. Honestly, given what this family is going through, the food is better than the other reviews are saying. Four stars, and please go support them.
cue: given what this family is going through, the food is better than the other reviews are saying
explanation: Linnea's own visit matches the complaints, but she rates the food higher because she feels for the owner. His situation is a reason for kindness, not evidence about the pasta.

whyNot.fal_red_herring: Linnea doesn't change the subject from the food; she lets sympathy for the owner raise her verdict on it.

passage:
Pavel: Your code change fails the checkout tests and doesn't handle expired cards. I can't approve it yet.
Nia: Expired cards are maybe 1% of orders. And I've been here until 10 every night this week, and I just found out my lease isn't being renewed. Can we please release it? I really need a win right now.
cue: I just found out my lease isn't being renewed
explanation: Nia makes one relevant point about how rare expired cards are, then leans on her rough week to get the code released. Her late nights and lease don't fix the failing checkout tests.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_emotion: Nia's appeal is specifically for sympathy over her personal hardship, not some other feeling like pride or outrage.

source: Builder Samuel Okoro · Larkmoor zoning hearing
passage: Before you vote on the variance, I want you to know who's behind this project. My family has run Okoro Builders for three generations. The last two years have been brutal: we laid off half our crew, and my father's health is failing. Yes, the building sits four feet closer to the creek than the floodplain rule allows. This variance is the difference between finishing and losing everything.
cue: we laid off half our crew, and my father's health is failing
explanation: Samuel asks the board to excuse a floodplain violation because of his family's hardships. The rule exists for flood safety, and his struggles don't change how close the building sits to the creek.

whyNot.fal_red_herring: His story isn't an unrelated detour; it's offered as the very reason to grant the variance, which makes it a plea for sympathy.

passage: People are tearing apart Dr. Aldana's report on the Brindle River cleanup, and it's hard to watch. Her funding was cut in the spring, she's been caring for her mother on top of running the lab, and she still got this done. The least we can do is give her findings the benefit of the doubt instead of nitpicking her sampling methods.
cue: The least we can do is give her findings the benefit of the doubt
explanation: Gail asks readers to accept Dr. Aldana's findings because of her personal struggles. Pushing through hardship is admirable, but it doesn't answer the questions about her sampling methods.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_emotion: Gail's case rests specifically on sympathy for Dr. Aldana's hardships, not on pride, fear or outrage.

title: Extension request: Lab 4 report
passage: Dear Dr. Ferreira, I'm requesting a one-week extension on the Lab 4 report due Friday. I was hospitalized Monday through Wednesday (discharge note attached), and the syllabus allows extensions of up to seven days for documented medical absences. I've already finished the data analysis, so a week is enough to complete the write-up. Thank you, Kai
cue: the syllabus allows extensions of up to seven days for documented medical absences
explanation: Kai's hospital stay is relevant because the syllabus makes documented illness the standard for extensions. He shows he meets that standard instead of asking for sympathy.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_pity: Kai's hardship is exactly what the rule asks about, and he documents it, so it's a reason, not a bid for sympathy.

source: Caseworker Imani Carter · Wrenford housing committee
passage: The emergency rent fund is for households facing eviction after a sudden loss of income. The Abebe family meets both conditions: Mr. Abebe was laid off in August, with the letter on file, and they received a notice to vacate on October 2. Their story is hard to hear, but that's not why I'm recommending approval. It's because they meet the fund's criteria.
cue: It's because they meet the fund's criteria.
explanation: Imani's case involves real hardship, but she ties it to the fund's written criteria and documents both. Need is the very thing this fund is meant to decide on.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_pity: The fund exists for this kind of hardship, and Imani shows the family meets its documented conditions instead of just evoking sympathy.
